sources.verifiedBoundary: Conditional writes test If-None-Match or If-Match during the write. Versioned-bucket checks concern current version; a delete marker has distinct behavior. This supports comparing public API semantics, not asserting our metadata protocol is S3.
Complete accepts ordered part identities/ETags; an initial HTTP 200 can still contain an embedded failure, so status line alone is not completed-object evidence.
Parts already in flight may still succeed after abort; cleanup can require repeated abort and ListParts verification.

Sorted-set scores exactly represent integers through inclusive ±2^53. Equal scores compare member bytes lexicographically. CH counts additions and actual changes, whereas GT restricts existing-score comparisons.
A Lua script runs without interleaving other server activity, and blocks the server. This does not supply cluster-wide commit, durability, or database coordination.

API v1 network retries retain one idempotency key and identical parameters within the first 24 hours; unresolved outcomes then require reconciliation. 500 may have side effects; a new key is unsafe while outcome remains unknown. API v2 has different behavior and a 30-day window.

API v1 caches the first result once execution begins, including 500; validation/concurrent pre-execution rejections are not cached. Keys can be pruned after at least 24 hours, then reuse can create a new request; parameter equality is checked.

Signature verification uses the raw body. Receivers must handle duplicate and unordered events. A local durable inbox is our design boundary, rather than an assertion of an upstream database transaction.

CHECK cannot guarantee conditions on other rows. A NULL predicate passes CHECK unless NOT NULL is explicit. Ledger balance and aggregate limits need a transactional writer/constraint protocol beyond per-line checks.
ZRANGE index stop is inclusive, REV reverses score and tie byte order. Reading bounded around-me rows in a script prevents interleaving, but cannot create a common cross-shard snapshot.

Haystack reduces per-photo metadata so lookups fit memory and data reads avoid extra metadata seeks; compact identity/offset/length and record checksums support the packing/validation explanation. This is the 2010 workload and design, not universal zero-I/O behavior.

f4 separates warm BLOBs by lower access/deletion rates and reduces effective replication cost using coding and failure-domain placement. The chapter explicitly supplies its own 4+2 teaching code and all-fragment publication policy, rather than claiming these are f4 or S3 internals.
